content.title: Where Raven Johnson, Madina Okot, Ta'Niya Latson got picked in 2026 WNBA Draft
content.text: Updated April 13, 2026, 10:36 p.m. ETSouth Carolina women's basketball had three players taken in the 2026 WNBA Draft on April 13.Raven Johnson and Madina Okot were drafted in the first round, with Ta'Niya Latson drafted in the second, adding to the long list of Dawn Staley that graduated into the WNBA.The draft is at The Shed at Hudson Yards in New York City.Before this year, Staley had 18 total players drafted out of South Carolina, 11 of whom came in the first round and two were No. 1 overall selections. Last year she had three players selected, all in the second round.Follow along for live updates from draft night. Ta'Niya Latson drafted No. 20 overall to the LA SparksThe third and final Gamecocks player to get off the board is Ta'Niya Latson who was drafted No. 20 overall by the LA Sparks. She will play with Sania Feagin, who played four years for Staley and was drafted last year by the Sparks. Madina Okot drafted No. 13 overall to the Atlanta DreamMadina Okot was the second player drafted from South Carolina, as she went No. 13 overall to the Atlanta Dream. Te-Hina Paopao and Allisha Gray are both on the Dream and both transferred into Staley's program like Okot did in college. Raven Johnson drafted No. 10 overall to the Indiana FeverRaven Johnson is the first South Carolina player drafted, as she goes 10th overall to the Indiana Fever. She'll reunite with her former teammate Aliyah Boston, who went first overall in 2023 to the Fever. Raven Johnson, Ta'Niya Latson, Madina Okot draft outfitsWith the carpet starting, players are beginning to arrive. Ta'Niya Latson is wearing a black sparkly dress. Raven Johnson is wearing a multi-patterned black, gray and white dress, and Madina Okot is wearing a light red/orange pinstripe suit.How many WNBA players has Dawn Staley produced?Staley has produced 18 WNBA draft selections since taking over the South Carolina program.A'ja Wilson was the first No. 1 overall pick in 2018, Aliyah Boston the second in 2022. South Carolina has produced 11 first-round picks total.Raven Johnson WNBA draft projectionsESPN - No. 7 to Portland FireThe Athletic - No.7 to Portland FireUSA TODAY - No. 9 to Washington MysticsTa'Niya Latson WNBA draft projectionsESPN - No. 13 to Atlanta DreamThe Athletic - No. 9 to Washington MysticsUSA TODAY - No. 6 to Toronto TempoMadina Okot WNBA draft projectionsESPN - No. 10 to Connecticut SunThe Athletic - No. 15 to Connecticut SunUSA TODAY - No. 13 to Atlanta DreamWhere is 2026 WNBA Draft?The draft is at The Shed at Hudson Yards in New York City.How many WNBA draft picks are in the first round?There are 15 picks in the first round. The first five picks were determined by a lottery based on teams that missed the playoffs last season, then two expansion teams in Toronto Tempo and Portland Fire pick sixth and seventh. The remaining order for each round is the inverse order of the standings from the 2025 regular season.Three rounds will be televised on April 13.Where to watch 2026 WNBA DraftTV: ESPN which is available on Fubo, which offers a free trialSteaming: ESPN+How to watch online: Watch ESPN (here's how to stream it live)What time does 2026 WNBA Draft start?Where: The Shed at Hudson Yards in New York CityDate: April 13Time: 7 p.m. ETCoverage begins at 6:30 pm ET on ESPN. What time is 2026 WNBA Draft red carpet?Before the draft begins, the WNBA has a "Orange Carpet Special" that begins at 5:30 p.m. ET and airs on ESPN2. Some draftees are interviewed on the carpet before the draft begins.Madina Okot stats, heightOkot is 6-foot-6 and played one season at South Carolina this year after transferring in from Mississippi State.Okot ended her college career averaging an SEC-best 10.6 rebounds along with 12.8 points per game for the Gamecocks. She shot a team-high 57.5% from the floor and finished third in the nation with 22 double-doubles this season.She averaged 1.4 blocks and 1.3 steals a game, and including her time in Starkville, will enter the WNBA preseason with a 60.6% career field goal percentage.Where is Madina Okot from?Okot is from Kenya. She started playing basketball six years ago and when she was 17, she played 3-on-3 basketball for Kenya's national team then went to Zetech University (also in Kenya) before moving to play for Mississippi State during the 2024-25 season.She transferred to South Carolina last offseason. On April 8 the program announced that the NCAA denied Okot another year of eligibility, giving her no choice but to declare for the WNBA draft after just two college seasons in the United States.Raven Johnson stats, heightJohnson is a 5-foot-9 point guard who spent five seasons in Columbia but only played four, as she tore her ACL two games into her freshman year in 2021.She averaged a career-high 9.9 points per game in her final season. She also averaged a career-high 5.1 assists and shot a career-best 48.6% from the floor and 39.9% from the 3-point line this year. On two-point shots, she shot 52.8%.Johnson leaves South Carolina holding the record for assist-to-turnover ratio (2.86), and finished second in games played (153), third in assists (612) and eighth in steals (232). Johnson won 94.2% of games in her career with South Carolina, finishing 145-9 in games she played in.Ta'Niya Latson stats, heightLatson is a 5-8 shooting guard who spent one season with South Carolina after three at Florida State.She averaged 14.1 points and shot a career-high 48.6% from the floor this season. She averaged five made field goals, taking eight two-point attempts a game and 2.3 from behind the 3-point line to go with 3.6 assists and 1.7 steals. She shot 80.3% from the free throw line and for the first time in her career she shot above 50% on two-pointers (52.3%).She also averaged a career-low 1.2 fouls a game.Did Raven Johnson and Ta'Niya Latson play high school basketball together?Latson is a year younger than Johnson but the two played three seasons together for Westlake in Atlanta and won three state championships.Johnson signed with South Carolina as the No. 2 recruit in the Class of 2021 and Latson transferred to American Heritage High School in Florida for her senior year.Lulu Kesin covers South Carolina athletics for The Greenville News and the USA TODAY Network.
